title: Rigveda 10.175: To the pressing stones
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.175: To the pressing stones: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.175 is a hymn of 4 verses addressed to the pressing stones. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 149v-150r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.175.1-4 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 33); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 150r
translation.original_text:
1pra vo̍ grāvāṇaḥ savi̱tā de̱vaḥ su̍vatu̱ dharma̍ṇā | dhū̱rṣu yu̍jyadhvaṁ sunu̱ta ||
2grāvā̍ṇo̱ apa̍ du̱cchunā̱m apa̍ sedhata durma̱tim | u̱srāḥ ka̍rtana bheṣa̱jam ||
3grāvā̍ṇa̱ upa̍re̱ṣv ā ma̍hī̱yante̍ sa̱joṣa̍saḥ | vṛṣṇe̱ dadha̍to̱ vṛṣṇya̍m ||
4grāvā̍ṇaḥ savi̱tā nu vo̍ de̱vaḥ su̍vatu̱ dharma̍ṇā | yaja̍mānāya sunva̱te ||
translation.text:
1MAY Savitar the God, O Stones, stir you according to the Law: Be harnessed to the shafts, and press.
2Stones, drive calamity away, drive ye away malevolence: Make ye the Cows our medicine.
3Of one accord the upper Stones, giving the Bull his bull-like strength, Look down with pride on those below.
4May Savitar the God, O Stones, stir you as Law commands for him Who sacrifices, pouring juice.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 150r (OPenn image 149, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.175.1 ‹-grāvāṇaḥ savitā devaḥ suvatu›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 150v, begins in RV 10.176.4 ‹ayam agnir uruṣyaty amṛtād›. Verses 10.175.1-4 end on this page; 10.175.1 begins on fol. 149v.
